content.text:
I fixed `saveAll` in `store.js`. It now waits for every write and rejects if any write fails.

**The bug:** `items.forEach(async ...)` discards the promises from each async callback. The function returned `items.length` immediately, so callers could get a result before any `db.put` had finished, and a failed write became an unhandled rejection instead of a rejection of `saveAll`.

**The fix:**
```js
async function saveAll(items, db) {
  await Promise.all(items.map((item) => db.put(item.id, item)));
  return items.length;
}
```

**Tests:** The existing test passed on the buggy code too, because its fake `put` writes synchronously and so hid the problem. I added two tests to `test/store.test.js`:
- **Slow writes:** `put` takes 20 ms, and the test checks that all three items are stored when `saveAll` resolves.
- **Failed write:** one `put` throws, and the test checks that `saveAll` rejects with that error.

🧾 1 receipt · npm test → # pass 3 (run after the edits: `# tests 3`, `# pass 3`, `# fail 0`)

🧾 allegedly · the new tests fail on the old `forEach` code · to check: copy the old `store.js` into a scratch directory next to the new test file and run `node --test`. I tried this, but the Bash call was denied by the permission mode, so I did not run it. I didn't try to get around the denial.

This is a standard-library-only Node project with no git repo, so I haven't checked how callers use `saveAll`. If they depend on the old early return, they will now wait for the writes to finish.
